title: Decision Reasons
description: Why trades were taken, how often each reason recurs, and what each one earned.

target.queryText:
SELECT MIN(t.executed_ts) AS time,
       i.symbol || ' ' || t.side || ' ' || SUM(t.quantity) || ' @ '
         || printf('%.2f', SUM(t.quantity * t.price) / SUM(t.quantity))
         || CASE WHEN n.sentiment IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ' - ' || n.sentiment END
         || CASE WHEN n.note IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ': ' || n.note END AS text,
       t.side || COALESCE(',' || n.sentiment, '') AS tags
FROM trade_note n
JOIN trade t ON t.id = n.trade_id
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = t.instrument_id
WHERE t.side = 'BUY'
GROUP BY i.symbol, t.session_date, t.side, COALESCE(t.order_id, 'at' || t.executed_ts), n.sentiment, n.note
ORDER BY MIN(t.executed_ts)
LIMIT 500

panels.title: How often each reason was used

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT reason_code AS "Reason", SUM(occurrences) AS "Times used"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC
targets.queryText:
SELECT reason_code AS "Reason", SUM(occurrences) AS "Times used"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC

panels.description:
How often each reason was recorded against a fill.

- **UNEXPLAINED** — a real category rather than a gap: a fill with no note, event or alert behind it.

panels.title: Where the reason came from

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT reason_source AS "Source", SUM(occurrences) AS "Times used"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_source
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC
targets.queryText:
SELECT reason_source AS "Source", SUM(occurrences) AS "Times used"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_source
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC

panels.description:
Where each recorded reason came from.

- **MANUAL** — what you typed.
- **EVENT** — a pattern the detector found.
- **ALERT** — something the system had just told you.

panels.title: Buy reasons vs sell reasons

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT reason_code AS "Reason",
       SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'BUY'  THEN occurrences ELSE 0 END) AS "Buys",
       SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN occurrences ELSE 0 END) AS "Sells"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC
targets.queryText:
SELECT reason_code AS "Reason",
       SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'BUY'  THEN occurrences ELSE 0 END) AS "Buys",
       SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN occurrences ELSE 0 END) AS "Sells"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC

panels.description:
The same reasons split by side, showing which get you into a position and which get you out.

A reason that only ever appears on one side is worth noticing.

panels.title: Reasons used per day

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', session_date) AS INTEGER) AS time,
       reason_code AS metric,
       SUM(occurrences) AS value
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY session_date, reason_code
ORDER BY session_date
targets.queryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', session_date) AS INTEGER) AS time,
       reason_code AS metric,
       SUM(occurrences) AS value
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY session_date, reason_code
ORDER BY session_date

panels.description:
How the reasons you record shift over time, one line per reason code.

**Notes** (cyan dashed lines) — notes tagged `BUY` or `SELL` on any symbol's chart. Hover a marker to read the note and see which symbol it was for.

**Noted calls** (light-blue buys, orange sells; dashed lines) — calls you documented with `trades note`, for every symbol. Hover a marker for the symbol, the sentiment and your note.

panels.title: Did the reason pay?

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT reason_code   AS "Reason",
       reason_source AS "Source",
       SUM(occurrences) AS "Times used",
       SUM(bet_amount)  AS "Bet amount",
       SUM(net_pnl)     AS "Net P&L",
       ROUND(SUM(net_pnl) / NULLIF(SUM(occurrences), 0), 2) AS "Net per use"
FROM v_reason_frequency
GROUP BY reason_code, reason_source
ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC
targets.queryText:

ORDER BY SUM(occurrences) DESC

panels.description:
Frequency says what you do most; this says whether it works.

A reason used often with a negative net is the one worth arguing with.
